EPIDEMIOLOGY PROFILE OF INJURIES OF ELITE AND SUB-ELITE MALE ARTISTIC GYMNASTS IN SOFIA, BULGARIA  

ABSTRACT Introduction: Artistic gymnastics is an Olympic sport in which male artistic gymnasts execute on six apparatuses. The number of weekly training sessions can reach to 12, with 36 hours overall load. Methodology: The study was conducted among 15 elite and 16 sub-elite gymnasts on international and national level from Sofia, Bulgaria. The participants completed a questionnaire about the type, severity, location, and causes for the appearance of injuries. Results: We calculated injury incidence at 93.33% for elite and 87.50% for sub-elite male artistic gymnasts. The injury rate for elite gymnasts was 2.19/1000 gymnastic exposures and 2.87 injuries per gymnast for the year. The injury rate for sub-elite gymnasts was 3.78/1000 gymnastic exposures and 2.13 injuries per gymnast for the year. The acute injuries prevailed in all participants. Shoulder is the most frequently injured anatomical location as a result of the exercises performed on rings and horizontal bar. Ankle is the next frequently traumatized location because of the exercises done on floor and vault (landing phase). Conclusions: Literature detailing injuries in male artistic gymnasts is scarce, which makes it relatively difficult to compare gender data. Injury rates in the male artistic gymnasts we studied fall within the range described in the sports literature.

Typically, for VIO, satisfying results have been accomplished due to the complementary sensing abilities of inertial measurement units (IMU) and cameras. However, this work primarily concentrates on the fusion of visual and inertial data, while the IMU inaccuracies are less regarded, especially for low-cost or poorly calibrated micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) IMU. Such inaccuracies may have a considerable impact on the VIO performance. In this study, we adjusted the IMU using camera support. The key attribute of the method is that we enhance the adjustment parameters (scale factor) from coarse to fine by combining the time domain with the frequency domain. The suggested method is to employ the time domain and frequency domain optimization to mitigate the large noise in the dynamic calibration process of the extremely low-cost sensor platform. The efficacy of this method is confirmed through experiments and simulations. The minimal calibration error 0.46% equivalent to the advanced work. By inputting the adjusted IMU into the VIO algorithm, the localization precision is enhanced by 9% to 15%. This method boosts the performance in the VIO algorithm which is equipped with the low-cost or poorly calibrated MEMS-IMU and decreases the hardware and deployment expenses of the system.

perturbations.b: Antifungal medication tolerance is a reaction distinct from resistance, in which cells grow slowly above the minimum inhibitory medication concentration (MIC). Here we found that the majority (69.2%) of 133 Candida albicans clinical isolates, including standard lab strain SC5314, demonstrated temperature-enhanced tolerance at 37°C and 39°C, and were not tolerant at 30°C. Other isolates were either always tolerant (23.3%) or never tolerant (7.5%) at these three temperatures, suggesting that tolerance requires different physiological mechanisms in different isolates. At supra-MIC fluconazole concentrations (8-128 μg/ml), tolerant colonies emerged swiftly at a frequency of ∼10−3. In liquid passages over a broader range of fluconazole concentrations (0.25-128 μg/ml), tolerance emerged quickly (within one passage) at supra-MIC concentrations. By contrast, resistance appeared at sub-MIC concentrations after 5 or more passages. Of 155 adaptors that evolved higher tolerance, all carried one of several recurrent aneuploid chromosomes, often including chromosome R, alone or in combination with other chromosomes. Furthermore, loss of these recurrent aneuploidies was associated with a loss of acquired tolerance, indicating that specific aneuploidies bestow fluconazole tolerance. Thus, genetic background and physiology, and the degree of medication stress (above or below the MIC) influence the evolutionary pathways and dynamics with which antifungal medication resistance or tolerance emerges.

Background: The objective of this study is to ascertain the correlation of neuroinflammatory response biomarkers neutrophil to lymphocyte ratio (NLR), neutrophil to platelet ratio (NPR) with risk elements, etiology, and prognosis in stroke victims.  
Methods: Cases diagnosed with ischemic stroke were enlisted in this study. Demographic information, comorbidities, laboratory results, carotid doppler ultrasonography, NIHSS (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) and MRS (modified rankin scale) scores of the cases were recorded. Afterwards, the cases were categorized into 3 groups (posterior circulation infarct, anterior circulation infarct, and lacunar infarct).  
Results: A total of 133 individuals, 65 female and 68 males, aged between 24 and 94 were included in this study. At the end of hospitalization, NLR (p=0.001) and NPR (p=0.007) were significantly found elevated in individuals with adverse functional outcome (MRS≥3) and those who perished compared to NLR (p=0.001) and NPR (p=0.008) in the favorable functional outcome group. The NLR cut-off value for adverse functional outcome (95% confidence interval lower limit of area-under-curve of ROC≥0.7) was determined to be 4.0.  
Conclusion: Elevated NLR and NPR values measured at first admission in individuals with acute ischemic stroke are strongly associated with adverse functional outcome and mortality, and NLR and NPR are significant prognostic biomarkers in individuals with acute ischemic stroke.

Bacillus Coagulans and its Spore as Potential Probiotics in the Creation of Innovative Shelf- Stable Foods

The synbiotic foods with therapeutic functions have been advantageous to gut health and immunity enhancement, including Bacillus coagulans as the probiotic microorganism. It is favored over other lactic acid bacteria (LAB) as it can generate spores. It is cultivated in the pH range of 5.5 to 6.2 and emits spores at 37 °C. These microbial spores can endure environments with high temperatures, acidic conditions, and salinity, making it a feasible probiotic organism for creation of innovative shelf-stable foods. It has become a crucial ingredient in the functional food industry due to its probiotic traits and significant resistance to stressful situations. For extensive commercial usage and a wide array of food applications, besides probiotic traits, a probiotic organism must be economical, practical, and remain viable throughout the processing, storage, and consumption. The non-spore- forming lactic acid bacteria can be employed to create probiotic products and fermented dairy products under regulated processing and storage circumstances. The spore- forming probiotic organism can be introduced into the human gut through innovative food products derived from cereals, legumes, fruits, and vegetables, confectionery products, and meat and non-dairy items. This has led to the advancement of practical and shelf-stable non-dairy probiotics. These non-dairy-based probiotics are less expensive, robust against various processing circumstances, high in bioactive elements, and can alleviate the risk of lifestyle diseases and diminish. Furthermore, lactose intolerance is related to the intake of dairy probiotics. Consequently, this review aimed to evaluate the deployment of probiotic Bacillus coagulans spores in emerging shelf-stable innovative non-dairy products with probiotic potential.

The original term “cytoprotection” was pioneered by Andre Robert who discovered the safety of the gastric mucosa by endogenous prostaglandins (PGs) stimulated by intragastric administration of “mild irritants” or by exogenous PGs used at dosages that induced this protective effect when administered in non-antisecretory doses. Later, most researchers focused on the mechanism and drug therapy of gastrointestinal injuries and chronic gastroduodenal ulcers, more relevant to clinical gastroenterology. Both safety and healing are universal and can affect other then digestive tissues and even body organs nowadays defined as “organoprotection.” Therefore, our current Research Topic was dedicated to the latest advancements in the field of injuries, safety and healing not only of gastrointestinal organs but also non-digestive cells and tissues. Wetland Water Level Forecasting Using Artificial Neural Networks—A Case Study in the Colombo Flood Control Area, Sri Lanka

Historically, wetlands have not been given much focus in terms of their worth due to the general public being oblivious. Nevertheless, wetlands are still jeopardized by many human activities, in addition to ongoing climate change. With these recent advancements, water level forecasting of wetlands has become a significant task in order to identify potential ecological harm and for the sustainable administration of wetlands. Therefore, this study recognized a dependable neural network model by which to forecast wetland water levels over the Colombo flood control area, Sri Lanka. This is the first study carried out using machine learning techniques in wetland water level forecasts in Sri Lanka. The model was developed with independent meteorological factors, including rainfall, evaporation, temperature, relative humidity, and wind velocity. The water levels measurements of prior years were used as dependent factors, and the analysis was based on a seasonal timeframe. Two neural network training algorithms, the Levenberg Marquardt algorithm (LM) and the Scaled Conjugate algorithm (SG), were used to model the nonlinear connection, while the Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Coefficient of Correlation (CC) were used as the performance metrics by which to understand the resilience of the model. In addition, uncertainty analysis was carried out using d-factor simulations. The performance metrics showed that the LM algorithm produced superior results by which to model the wetland water level ahead of the SC algorithm, with a mean squared error of 0.0002 and a coefficient of correlation of 0.99. In addition, the computational efficiencies were exceptional in the LM algorithm compared to the SC algorithm in terms of the forecasting of water levels. LM demonstrated 3–5 epochs, whereas SC demonstrated 34–50 epochs of computational efficiencies for all four seasonal forecasts. However, the d-factor demonstrated that the results were not within the cluster of uncertainty. Therefore, the overall results imply that the Artificial Neural Network can be successfully utilized to forecast the wetland water levels, which is immensely important in the management and preservation of the wetlands.

Biogenic Production of Thiosulfate from Organic and Inorganic Sulfur Substrates for Utilization to Gold Leaching

Gold extraction and processing is an endeavor with significant environmental influence due to the low quantity of gold in ore deposits and chemical resistance to most substances. Over 75% of gold is leached from ores using cyanide, however less harmful lixiviants have been suggested in the literature. Thiosulfate is one of these substitute reagents, but high reagent usage has hindered acceptance in mining operations. Reducing the expense and effect of thiosulfate manufacture is a method to decrease the cost of reagent usage during leaching. The aim of this research was to assess the feasibility of leaching gold from ore with biogenic thiosulfate. Biogenic thiosulfate was generated using a marine methylotroph microorganism from three sources: sodium sulfide, elemental sulfur, and dimethyl sulfide for use in bioleaching. The various sources were assessed to determine conversion efficacy from the sulfur source to biogenic thiosulfate and confirmed by titration and ion chromatography. Optimal situations for conversion to thiosulfate were established to be in the spectrum of pH = 7–8, 25–30 °C, with sodium sulfide as a source in a sealed environment to prevent sulfide from escaping as hydrogen sulfide gas. An oxide gold ore with a quality of 4.02 g/t was chosen as a gold source for leaching tests. The leaching of gold utilizing the biogenic thiosulfate was contrasted with chemical thiosulfate solutions under experimental situations of pH = 9.5, 50 mg/L copper, 500 RPM mixing, and 0.1 L/min air. The efficacy of gold bioleaching was quantified using flame atomic absorption spectroscopy and fire assay. Gold extraction efficacies ranging from 20–60% were attained using the biogenic thiosulfate, and 27–77% with sodium thiosulfate solutions, correspondingly. It was concluded that the sodium sulfide source was optimal for generating higher biogenic thiosulfate concentrations and leaching efficacy.

The Lord’s Supper is likely one of the most crucial components in Christianity. However, churches presently observe two extreme perspectives in engaging with the Lord’s Supper: one that over-sacralizes the ritual as something mystical or magical while the other merely views it as a ceremony or memorial. While both concepts are not incorrect in some sense, the ritual in fact falls somewhere in the center. Eucharist included two significant dimensions: it is a feast, and it is a “sacrificial” feast. The ordinary and the spiritual facets both exist within the eucharist.  
In the accounts of the Last Supper, Jesus consumed the Passover “feast” with His disciples and reinstated it. From that point on, the early church commemorated the Lord’s Supper, gathering and breaking bread in homes, which was thereafter known as agape—a love celebration. However, what we observe in today’s Lord’s Supper is nowhere near the original Last Supper or the early Christian agape celebration. It transforms into a ritual without a feast; a celebration without a banquet. It is ironic that the so-called “supper” only involves a wafer-like bread and a really small cup of wine. It is the absence of a “feast” that this ritual becomes increasingly detached. The Lord’s Supper becomes challenging to comprehend because of the focus on its sanctity. The ritual remains a ceremony as the “sacred” is divided from the “secular”.  
It is the argument of this study that the division of the love celebration from the ritual of the Lord’s Supper that renders it insignificant. This study seeks to reveal the context and history of the Lord’s Supper, particularly the importance of a feast or meal in the eucharist, and how it was lost in the passage of time. We will see that it is in the context of a feast that the early church commemorates the eucharist, a thanksgiving in the form of a love celebration. It is in the context of a feast that Jesus unveiled His body and blood in the Last Supper. It is in the context of a feast that God instructed the Israelites to observe the Passover. When we engage with the Lord’s Table without a proper feast, the consumption of the “bread” and “wine” without context becomes a ritual without truth.  
Finally, recommendations are made to better engage with the Lord’s Table, and ideally restore the significance and essence of the ceremony.

1077 THE FUNCTION OF MILITARY NURSE IN THE CARDIAC AMBULATORY OF MILITARY HOSPITAL IN MILAN

 Military nurses have a crucial role in taking care of all military personnel, both in preventive medicine and direct health care, to be effective and skilled during his duty, both in national settings and in operations abroad.  
 The military nursing, in a cardiac ambulatory atmosphere, aim to ensure, collaborating with the cardiologist medical officer, the fitness for military service, i.e. the possession of physical and psycho-attitudinal requirements needed to perform military service that necessitates specific and dynamic efforts that could stimulate determined organs or body systems.  
 Among the various visits that the military personnel have to attend, the cardiac ambulatory is specialized in: Personnel selection for volunteers recruitment;Evaluation for those soldiers that experienced cardiovascular diseases that have to be visited by Military Legal Medical Facilities;Medical periodic visits for military personnel on duty to check the maintenance of psycho-physical requirements;Medical visits for military personnel ready to be deployed in missions abroad or that are just returning from them;Definition of diagnostic protocol and evaluation of those soldiers that experienced cardiovascular disease.  
 In details, the primary specific competences of the military nurse in a cardiology ambulatory are: assessment of cardiovascular health (cardiac anamnesis and physical evaluation), diagnostic exams procedures (ECG, assisting in sonography examination, positioning and management of Holter for blood pressure and ECG, cardiopulmonary test), evaluation of medication prescription per cardiovascular disease (antihypertensives, antiplatelet agents, antithrombotic, thrombolytics, antiarrhythmics, with focus on the initiation of therapy, mode of action and interactions).  
 The military nurse in cardiovascular ambulatory, in addition to the numerous activities, typical of being a warrant officer deployable in national activities or in operations abroad, must acquire competences and knowledge specific for cardiac setting, through basic training courses, continuous medical education, ensuring a constant synergy with all the équipe members, even at international level, also acting independently in all those complex situations that may arise to meet patients’ needs.

Differential Expression of Inflammationrafts in Macrophage Foam Cells and in Nonfoamy Macrophages in Atherosclerotic Lesions.

BACKGROUND  
Reprogramming of monocytes and macrophage manifests in hyperinflammatory reactions and chronification of inflammation in atherosclerosis. Recent studies concentrated on epigenetic, transcriptional, and metabolic modifications that characterize trained immunity. However, the underlying effector mechanisms driving the hyperinflammatory response of reprogrammed macrophages remain unclear. We hypothesized that the plasma membrane of atherosclerotic lesion macrophages undergoes reprogramming to maintain inflammationrafts, enlarged lipid rafts (LR) serving as a platform for assembly of inflammatory receptor complexes.

METHODS  
Single-cell suspensions from the aortae of Western diet-fed Ldlr-/- mice were gated for BODIPY-high foamy and BODIPY-low nonfoamy F4/80 macrophages by flow cytometry. Inflammationrafts were characterized by increased levels of LR, TLR4 localization to LR, TLR4 dimers, and the proximity between TLR2, TLR1, and CD36. In a cellular model of trained immunity, LR, TLR4 dimers, and the inflammatory response were measured in bone marrow-derived macrophages subjected to a 24-hour treatment with lipopolysaccharide or OxLDL, followed by a 6-day wash-out period.

RESULTS  
Nonfoamy macrophages, which constituted ≈40% of macrophages in atherosclerotic lesions, expressed significantly higher levels of LR and TLR4 dimers, as well as proximity ligation signals for TLR4-LR, TLR2-CD36, and TLR2-TLR1 complexes, compared with foamy macrophages. These inflammationraft measures associated, to a different degree, with plasma cholesterol and inflammatory cytokines, as well as the size of the atherosclerotic lesions and necrotic cores. The bone marrow-derived macrophages trained with lipopolysaccharide simulated nonfoamy atherosclerotic lesion macrophages and continued to express inflammationrafts and inflammatory genes for 6 days after lipopolysaccharide removal and displayed a hyperinflammatory response to Pam3CSK4, a TLR2/TLR1 agonist. perturbations.a: Market evaluation of medicinal products with nimesulide
perturbations.b: nimesulide-containing pharmaceutical products are the most favored non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents which have been extensively utilized in practice for numerous years. This active compound belongs to selective cyclooxygenase 2 blockers is a strong pain alleviator distinguished by a swift therapeutic impact compared to other analgesics. Despite the conflicting literature evidence of the past decades concerning the employment of nimesulide due to its hepatotoxic impact, nimesulide medications persist as a priority in the management of patients with pain syndrome of diverse genesis globally. At present, nimesulide is manufactured worldwide in various dosage forms. Some investigations in recent years have demonstrated its antitumor impact which has resulted in the emergence of new specific forms with nimesulide such as microgranules, microspheres, nanoparticles with targeted delivery. Therefore, the aim of the examination was to evaluate the Ukrainian pharmaceutical market of products with the nimesulide active ingredient by dosage forms, producers; to determine the quality composition of original and generic medications. The subjects of the research were pharmaceutical products containing nimesulide listed in Ukraine. The research was conducted by analyzing register data, utilizing methods of grouping, comparison, graphic analysis, and generalization. In the study, an assessment of medicines with nimesulide by dosage form and producers was executed. The excipients composition of reference medications for nimesulide granules for oral suspension was also studied. It was found that 32 medicines with nimesulide are listed in Ukraine, including 28 mono-preparations. A considerable portion of medicinal products with nimesulide are solid dosage forms, namely tablets (47 %) or granules for oral solution (22 %) which consist of 100 mg of nimesulide. It was found that there are no nimesulide in the form of extended-release tablets on the domestic market. Nimesulide drug products from foreign producers are predominant (59.38 %), India holds a leading position (50 %). Granules are mainly manufactured by foreign producers that supports the practicality of developing a domestic generic product. The original product is Aulin, granules for oral solution, “Angelini Pharma”, Czech Republic. Variances in the qualitative composition of excipients of the original and generic products which are present on the Ukrainian market were noted. The formulation of products more frequently includes sucrose as filler, сetomacrogol 1000, liquid glucose spray-dried, maltodextrin, sodium saccharin, anhydrous citric acid, orange flavoring, corn starch, or Aerosil 200. As such, the viability of development of domestic medicinal product in the form of prolonged-release tablets and granules was validated; the original product of nimesulide granules for oral solution was identified and the qualitative composition of the reference medications was established.

Intima-Media Thickness and Pulsatility Index of Common Carotid Arteries in Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients with Diabetes Mellitus

Ultrasonic parameters such as the common carotid artery (CCA) pulsatility index (PI) and CCA intima-media thickness (IMT) have been linked to an increased mortality and risk of recurrent stroke, respectively. We theorized that these ultrasonic parameters may be beneficial for monitoring diabetic patients after an acute stroke. We evaluated retrospective data of consecutive acute ischemic stroke patients from the ASTRAL registry who underwent pre-cerebral ultrasonic assessment within 7 days of symptom onset. We contrasted clinical, demographic, radiological and ultrasonic parameters in diabetic versus non-diabetic patients (univariable and multivariable analyses) and the relationship of these parameters with CCA PI and CCA IMT. We examined 1507 carotid duplex ultrasound investigations from patients with a median age of 74 years. Cardiovascular co-morbidities, including hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, obstructive sleep apnea syndrome, higher body-mass index (BMI) and peripheral artery disease, were linked to diabetes mellitus (DM). Diabetics were more frequently under antiplatelet treatment and had atrial fibrillation at admission. Diabetic patients displayed an increased CCA PI and IMT in line with more atherosclerotic changes on acute CTA compared to non-diabetic patients. Taking IMT as the dependent variable in a second analysis, DM, higher age, hypertension, smoking and CCA PI were associated with greater IMT. Taking CCA PI as the dependent variable in a third analysis, DM, higher age and higher NIHSS at admission were associated with elevated CCA PI values. Increased IMT was also associated with higher PI. We demonstrate that CCA PI and IMT are higher in diabetic patients in the initial week after an initial stroke.
